description: The brief's central premise does not match the data. It specifies at least 200 impulses, threshold impulse detection, coherent averaging and ERA on impulse responses; run 306428 is in fact a stepped-sine sweep, 18 steps from 3 to 20 Hz at 1 Hz, 30 s each, repeated 13 times. There are no impulses to detect. The spreadsheet's word 'impulse' denotes the shaker test, not a transient.
how_caught: Decoded ch1111 (shaker force) and took the Welch peak frequency and RMS in 5 s blocks over the whole run; found 237 discrete frequency groups matching the spreadsheet description
resolution: Open, escalated to Vivek as a gate decision. SPEC.md deliberately not drafted until the method is reset; stepped-sine FRF estimation is the natural substitute and still answers the modal question.

description: The vibes WriteTimestreamsFromDAQ.cpp isBadChannel() excludes channels 938-945 and 968-975 for any run above 303060. Run 306428 qualifies and ch 975, the channel Vivek asked for, is the last channel of that range. The samples are present in the RDCF, so this is a software exclusion in the lab's denoising code rather than missing data.
how_caught: Read the bad-channel rule in the vibes source, then confirmed Channel0975 is a live branch in the QRDCF
resolution: RESOLVED empirically, as Vivek directed. In quiet run RUNB ch975's 1-50 Hz noise power is 28.1 against a median of 5.46 over the 52 tower-19 bolometers: 5.2x the median but only rank 45/52, i.e. the 8th noisiest, with seven channels worse (ch961 at 42.9x the median). The vibes-excluded set (938-945, 968-975) has median 6.45 against 5.26 for the rest, a ratio of 1.22, so the rule does not select a noisy group and is not a quality cut. ch975 is usable but is not the best sole headline channel; all 52 are extracted. Separately, ch975 is the primary channel of the WitnessDenoise S4D work, a denoising project, which may be why it was chosen.

description: Two live credentials sit in files a demo would plausibly display: a commented-out but unexpired API bearer token in a shell startup file, and a database password in plaintext in a project setup script that the environment-sourcing step reads. PS1 also carries username and hostname, against the brief's Step 5 instruction.
how_caught: Encountered while reading .bashrc for the DIANA path and the vibes setup.sh for the install location, with no recording open
resolution: Not leaked: no recording was open and neither secret is reproduced in the log or results. Mitigations proposed to Vivek before rec_01_graph (set PS1, source DIANA off camera, do not display those two files on camera, rotate the token).

description: First pass of the RUNA step map omitted an amplitude cut, so three shaker-off segments where the FFT peak lands on ambient noise (force RMS 3.8-5.5 mV) were counted as sweep steps. That put the frequency sequence out of order and inflated the proposed 2.5-9.5 Hz extraction window to the whole 48,800 s run.
how_caught: Monotonicity sanity check on the recovered step sequence: frequency differences ranged -14.4 to +2.9 Hz for what must be a monotonic sweep
resolution: Fixed by requiring force RMS at or above 10 mV. 161 shaker-on steps, strictly monotonic 1.00 to 20.00 Hz. Caught before the design document was written, so no external cost.

description: The extraction writer cannot compile against the local $VIBES checkout, which is at master of 2025-08-02 and lacks src/VibesUtil.hh; no built binary exists anywhere in the user trees. how_caught: Vivek volunteered that the repository had moved to <INTERNAL_GITLAB_REMOTE>

description: Closed-form prediction of the extraction window from the nominal sweep parameters (f = 1.0 + 0.1k Hz at t = 250 + 250k s) gave t = [4000, 21500] s, short by 250 s at the upper edge. The run contains a 225 s shaker dropout at t = 1275-1500 s which shifts every later step by one dwell period.
how_caught: Measured the step map from ch1111 instead of trusting the arithmetic, then compared the two
resolution: Measured map adopted as the authority: t = [3990, 21760] s with 10 s margin. The dropout is recorded as a bad interval in data/meta.json. Had the arithmetic been trusted, the highest-frequency step of the band would have been silently truncated.

description: The CUORE DB endpoint advertised by cuoresw/setup.sh, <internal DB host>:5432, refuses connections. The only reachable endpoint is an override hand-added to the old $VIBES/setup.sh. The vibes Makefile regenerates setup.sh from a template with no DB override, so a fresh clone plus make silently loses the working endpoint and would fail later as an opaque bookkeeping lookup error.
how_caught: TCP connect test to both candidate endpoints before building anything, rather than after a failed run
resolution: Mitigated in extract/vibes_env.sh: the four CUORE_DB_* variables are re-imported at run time from the old checkout's setup.sh, so the password stays in the one file it already lives in and is never copied into this project, printed or logged.

description: First version of extract/extract_step1.sh used 'set -uo pipefail'. Sourcing cuoresw/setup.sh under set -u is fatal in a non-interactive shell because it reads unset variables, so the script exited immediately and silently, producing no output and no error message at all.
how_caught: Dry run of the extraction plan returned completely empty output instead of the expected command list
resolution: Fixed: dropped set -u in the driver and bracketed the source with set +u and restore in vibes_env.sh. Dry run then verified 283 channel-extractions across six run/window combinations.

description: uproot 4.3.7 in the pyR conda environment cannot read QRDCF waveform branches. It opens the file and lists the Channel0975 branch hierarchy, but every array read fails with AttributeError: 'DetachedFile' object has no attribute 'decompression_executor', via full branch path, nested navigation and tree.arrays alike.
how_caught: Benchmarked uproot against a C6 partial after Vivek suggested it might be faster than the DIANA path

Consistent with the existing uproot code in CUORE_SHRED, which reads a simpler non-QRDCF ROOT product and whose own docstring notes CUORE objects uproot cannot deserialize. Verifier independence will come from its own reader against the .bin files instead.

description: The ch975 outlier test in extract/sanity_step1.py used a MAD-based robust z score on the 1-50 Hz noise power of the 52 bolometers. That distribution is heavily right-skewed (median 5.46, mean 20.2, max 234.4), so the MAD-sigma is set by the dense core and anything in the upper tail scores above 3 automatically. The check reported FAIL for ch975 at z = +4.75 when the channel is merely 8th noisiest of 52.
how_caught: Characterised the full distribution and ch975's rank before reporting the FAIL, rather than reporting the FAIL as a result
resolution: The FAIL is an artifact of the statistic, not a property of the channel. Rank and percentiles are reported instead of a z score. The underlying question, E007, is resolved: ch975 is usable.

description: The orchestrator stated in extract/SHRED_COMPAT.md that the S4D encoder named in the brief's Step 6 'does not exist on this system' and that Step 6 model 2 was 'a build, not an import'. The claim was based on searching only ~/CUORE_SHRED and ~/Denoising. It is wrong: ~/ML_denoising_ssm/DenoisingAux/ holds a mature WitnessDenoise project implementing S4DDenoiser1D (bidirectional diagonal S4D, about 70k parameters) with a 1 kHz-to-200 Hz decimated core, plus the RootReader the brief names, and ch975 is its primary channel.
how_caught: Vivek pointed to the directory the orchestrator's search had never covered
resolution: SHRED_COMPAT.md carries a dated correction at the top and a rewritten section 4; the original wording is preserved verbatim in AGENT_GRAPH_LOG.md. Step 6 model 2 is reclassified as data preparation against a tested pipeline rather than a model build, which makes it materially more feasible.

description: GetAllTriggersByTower exits 0 and writes a structurally correct ChannelRunData_tower19.root, but every trigger list in it is empty (50 of 52 channels log 'we found 0 triggers'), while the tool's own stdout reports 'For flag 2 inserting 4882 triggers' for each channel. Two code paths: the flag lists go into myFlagTrigs while the written myTrigs comes from GetTriggerValues, which returns nothing. The effect is that the pulser is invisible in the file any downstream validity rule would read.
how_caught: Read the written file back with CUORE_SHRED rootmeta's own byte parser instead of trusting exit code 0
resolution: Worked around by reading the RdcfTriggerList objects straight from the last RDCF partial with a purpose built src/DumpTriggers.cpp. Whether the omission is deliberate (pulser flag discarded on purpose) is unknown and worth raising with the tool's author; either way the pulser must be masked explicitly.

description: Every bolometer carries a deterministic pulser at exactly 0.1000 Hz (4882 flag-2 triggers, 10.0000 s spacing, synchronous across channels, 1777 inside the extraction window). Its spectral comb sits on every multiple of 0.1 Hz, and every drive frequency used (2.5 to 9.5 Hz) is such a multiple. Worse, step boundaries are at multiples of 250 s and 250/10 = 25 exactly, so the pulser arrives at an identical phase relative to every step boundary and coherent step-onset averaging would accumulate it coherently, producing a repeatable transient indistinguishable from a structural step response that looks better the more steps are averaged.
how_caught: Dumped the trigger times directly from the RDCF after the regeneration tool wrote empty lists, then compared the pulser period against the frequency-step period
resolution: Open, to be written into SPEC.md as a required mitigation: mask a window around each of the 1777 pulser times, or offset step-onset windows by a non-multiple of 10 s, or notch the comb. H1 referenced to the force channel is unbiased by output noise so the primary FRF survives, but coherence must be reported per frequency. The critic will be given the pulser times so it can test whether any claimed mode or step response is phase-locked to 10 s rather than to the drive.

description: the shared home filesystem was at 85.1% of its 40 GiB quota (34.04 GiB used, ~6 GiB free) while the converted arrays total 6.2 GiB. Writing data/ into the project on home, as the brief's layout implies, would have filled the quota to essentially 100%, and a mid-write quota failure would have left a half-converted dataset and a wedged home directory hours before the deadline.
how_caught: Checked showquota and df before starting the conversion rather than after it failed
resolution: data/arrays made a symlink to <scratch>/CUORE_ImpulsePilot_data, so the project layout and all relative paths are unchanged while bulk lives on scratch; small metadata stays on home. Home usage after conversion unchanged at 85.1%.

description: SPEC.md and data/meta.json both described the ADC-to-mV factor as carried over from the aux channels and unverified for bolometers, implying an absolute-scale uncertainty on every bolometer amplitude. In fact 8.0108642578125e-02 is exactly 21000/2**18, the LSB of a +/-10.5 V 18-bit digitiser, so it is a DAQ-board property identical for all channels and the arrays are exactly mV at the ADC input.
how_caught: Vivek asked whether the uncertainty could be resolved, which prompted testing the number against candidate full-scale/bit combinations instead of treating it as an opaque constant
resolution: SPEC.md 2.1 item 3 rewritten: scale exact at the ADC, channel_gain.csv to be reported in mV at the ADC input and labelled so, claims of bolometer volts/temperature/energy forbidden without asking. The genuinely undetermined per-channel front-end gain is in the DB and is not needed, since all spec quantities are scale-free. meta.json provenance string still to be corrected before dispatch.

description: Every timestamp heading in AGENT_GRAPH_LOG.md after about 02:40 UTC was overstated by up to 122 minutes. After the first two entries the orchestrator wrote plausible clock times from its own sense of progress instead of calling date, and the drift compounded. True elapsed at graph dispatch was 131 min, not the 253 min the headings implied. Entry ordering and the per-item cost_min estimates are unaffected; the absolute headings are not trustworthy.
how_caught: The dispatch banner printed a real date -u of 04:18:07Z alongside a log entry headed 06:20Z written moments earlier
resolution: Correction entry appended (nothing edited, per the append-only rule). New convention: every heading timestamp comes from date -u at the moment of writing. Anchors for the cost table: session start 02:07Z, graph dispatch 04:18Z. Also withdraws the orchestrator's earlier recommendation to drop Step 6, which rested on the wrong elapsed figure: the true position is 2.18 h of a 5 h budget used with about 11.7 h to the deadline.

description: data/meta.json's amplitude_constant field stated that measured force varies '~25% across frequency' and that the drive repeats to 0.1-0.2%, presenting both as properties of run RUNA. Both belonged to run 306428 and were carried over when the pilot switched runs. In RUNA the force RMS actually spans 365.21 to 1521.01 mV, a factor 4.16, and contains step discontinuities of +71% (5.4 to 5.5 Hz) and -32% (7.4 to 7.5 Hz) that are more consistent with a reference-channel range or amplifier change than with shaker response.
how_caught: The independent verifier read data/steps.csv against meta.json's claim and found the excursion and the two one-step jumps, while blocked from doing any numerical analysis
resolution: Verified by the orchestrator, then meta.json and SPEC.md section 4.4 both rewritten: the 306428 figures are attributed to 306428, the 4.16 factor and the two discontinuities are stated for RUNA, and both agents are now told to form every transfer function as a strict ratio to ch1111 on the same step so an instrumental gain change cancels. Reported to the critic.

description: The verifier's sandbox settings file carried a deny list and no allow list. A headless claude -p session cannot answer an approval prompt, so every Write and every interpreter invocation was refused and the node produced none of its five deliverables and no log, while exiting 0 and printing its completion marker. The isolation mechanism worked and simultaneously rendered the node useless.
how_caught: The verifier reported the blocker explicitly rather than fabricating output; the orchestrator then confirmed by checking for the deliverable files instead of trusting exit code 0
resolution: Fixed: 16 allow rules added (Write/Edit/Read under verify/, Read on the two data directories, python3 and the pyR python, read-only shell tools) with the 12 deny rules retained and still taking precedence. Verifier re-dispatched. Lesson for the report: an exit code and a DONE marker are not evidence of work.

description: data/steps.csv published 25 s FFT bin centres as measured drive frequencies, so every value was quantised to 0.04 Hz and the column alternated +0.08/+0.12 Hz instead of a uniform 0.1 Hz. The stated band 2.52-9.52 Hz was wrong for the same reason; it is 2.50-9.50 Hz.
how_caught: The verifier noticed every frequency was an exact multiple of 0.04 Hz, one 25 s DFT bin, and inferred a true 0.1 Hz grid rounded to the estimator's resolution
resolution: steps.csv rewritten: each step's frequency measured over its full 250 s dwell by parabolic interpolation on the log-magnitude spectrum, about 4 mHz, plus an f_drive_hz_nominal column. Band corrected to 2.50-9.50 Hz throughout meta.json and SPEC.md.

description: From the quantised steps.csv the verifier inferred the drive grid might be 2.52+0.1k, hence f mod 0.1 = 0.02 Hz, which would place the drive frequencies about five 250 s bins off the pulser comb and make SPEC section 4.1's masking requirement too pessimistic. The inference was wrong: the grid is 2.5+0.1k.
how_caught: Measured the drive frequency on ch1111 over each full dwell at about 4 mHz resolution; the grid is f_k = 2.5+0.1k Hz with max deviation 0.00017 Hz, so f mod 0.1 < 0.0002 Hz
resolution: Refuted and recorded. Drive frequencies ARE multiples of 0.1 Hz, there is no frequency separation to exploit, and time-domain masking remains mandatory. SPEC 4.1 kept and strengthened with the measured numbers. Mitigating note: the verifier itself flagged that this had to be measured off ch1111 rather than assumed, so it proposed the test that refuted its own hypothesis.

description: data/steps.csv was rewritten in response to the verifier's quantisation finding while the analyst was mid-run against the old version. The analyst had read the old frequencies (2.52, 2.72, ...), reported a frequency discrepancy against them, then had to log a retraction when the file changed under it. A shared input was mutated during a running phase.
how_caught: The analyst noticed the file's mtime had changed (21:23:45 PDT) and reported it, withdrawing its own earlier finding
resolution: Lesson applied immediately, not deferred: two further shared-input corrections are pending (steps.csv t_start values, E029; PT fundamental in meta.json, E028) and the verifier is still running against both files. Neither will be touched until it finishes; both are recorded and will be applied at reconciliation, where the discrepancy is evidence rather than a moving target. A shared input is frozen for the duration of a phase.

description: The brief specifies pulse-tube lines at 'multiples of 1.4 Hz' and the orchestrator propagated that into meta.json, SPEC.md and the critic's check list. The true fundamental is 1.39443 Hz. The 0.4% error reaches 33 mHz at the 6th harmonic, comparable to the +/-50 mHz mode-frequency uncertainty, so a PT-versus-mode coincidence test built on 1.4 Hz can both miss real coincidences and manufacture false ones.
how_caught: The analyst measured the comb at 2.789/4.183/5.578/6.972/8.367 Hz and fitted a 1.39443 Hz fundamental, then the orchestrator confirmed it independently on quiet3 at 1.29 mHz resolution: residuals <= 0.2 mHz against 1.39443, versus -11 to -33 mHz against 1.4 Hz
resolution: Confirmed. The critic must use 1.39443 Hz. meta.json and SPEC.md corrections are deferred until the verifier finishes, per E027. Also retracts an earlier orchestrator claim that shaker-off peaks at 4.20 and 5.56 Hz were independent support for 1.4 Hz multiples: those came from 25 s FFTs with 0.04 Hz bins, which cannot distinguish 4.183 from 4.200.

description: data/steps.csv t_start values are late by 5.96-6.54 s (mean 6.34 s). The boundaries were taken from 25 s block edges, so each is the first block in which the dominant frequency had ALREADY changed, lagging the true boundary by up to 25 s. The analyst's recovered first boundary is run t = 4008.69 s with period 249.9994 s.
how_caught: The analyst recovered the boundaries itself, as SPEC section 3 instructed, and reported the systematic offset against steps.csv rather than adopting the published values
resolution: The analyst's boundaries are the better values and it used them. steps.csv correction deferred until the verifier finishes, per E027. Knock-on: the '25 s of shaker-off data at array t = 0-25 s' that the verifier derived from steps.csv is really about 18.7 s.

description: SPEC.md section 3 asks for responses.npz covering 'all 71 bolometer-plus-aux channels'. That 71 is arithmetic carried over from the original brief's 52 bolometers + 19 aux; this pilot extracted 26 aux, so the real count is 78.
how_caught: The analyst stated in its hand-back that it processed 78 channels, not the 71 SPEC.md gives, and named the discrepancy rather than silently following either number
resolution: The analyst's 78 is correct and it processed all of them, so no result is affected. SPEC.md wording to be corrected at reconciliation, per the E027 freeze.

description: Not every on-screen marker printed during rec_01_graph reached the .cast file. '=== GRAPH: analyst + verifier dispatched ===' is absent as a contiguous string although it was printed in the same command as the 'RECORDING CHECKPOINT' marker that did land. tmux pipe-pane captures only what the pane displays, and the TUI did not render every line of that tool output. The brief's requirement that the video be cuttable by searching the cast for marker text is only partly met for this segment.
how_caught: Parsed rec_01_graph.cast after stopping it and searched for each marker string, instead of assuming printed equals recorded
resolution: Procedure changed for the remaining segments: print each marker in its own minimal command and verify it is present in the cast afterwards. rec_01_graph still contains RECORDING CHECKPOINT, VERIFIER START, VERIFIER COMPLETE and === DONE ===, so it remains cuttable, just not at the dispatch line. No credential string appears in the cast.

description: SPEC.md section 4.3 made the prescribed damping upper limit 0.1/(2 f0) available without requiring a node to first ATTEMPT a measurement and justify falling back to it. The verifier consequently reported all 11 of its modes with zeta exactly equal to the formula and zeta_is_upper_limit true, contributing no independent damping information, while fully satisfying the spec. The cross-method damping comparison the brief asks for is therefore vacuous.
how_caught: Checked whether the verifier's zeta column was a measurement by testing every row against 0.1/(2 f0); all 11 matched to within 5e-6, and f0_err was the 0.0500 floor on every row
resolution: Open, and a limitation to state plainly in PROCESS_REPORT.md rather than paper over: the graph produced one measured damping set (analyst ring-down) and one set of formula limits, not two independent estimates. Correct spec wording would have been: attempt a measurement, report it with its uncertainty, and if you fall back to the prescribed limit, say which measurement you tried and why it failed.

description: The E031 entry mis-diagnosed the recording. It concluded from a search over the escape-stripped output stream that markers were not rendered and implied the capture was defective. The cast is in fact clean (5325 distinct fully-rendered lines); the orchestrator's analysis had stripped cursor-positioning escapes from a stream whose structure is cursor motion and overwrite, making substring search meaningless. The real cause of the one missing marker is that Claude Code displayed only the echoed command for that call, truncated at the 120-column pane width immediately after '=== GRAPH', and never displayed its stdout.
how_caught: Vivek asked what had actually been recorded, which forced a proper replay through a VT screen model instead of a substring search over stripped text
resolution: Wrote tools/cast_render.py (minimal VT100) and dumped recordings/rec_01_graph.txt. Correct rule recorded: a marker printed as stdout of a long compound command may never be displayed, so each marker must be the only content of a short command and must be verified in the cast afterwards. Supersedes E031's diagnosis; E031's procedural fix stands and is strengthened.

description: The critic node could not write critic/REPORT.md, reporting that its environment forbids writing report .md files, so its deliverable existed only in its hand-back message. It also noted that the ../AGENT_GRAPH_LOG.md path in the brief's agent definition does not resolve from the project root, which is correct for a node working in analysis/ or verify/ but wrong for one invoked at the root.
how_caught: The critic stated the blocker in its hand-back rather than silently dropping the deliverable
resolution: Orchestrator transcribed the hand-back verbatim into critic/REPORT.md with a provenance header naming the transcription and the audit result, so the file is the critic's content and not the orchestrator's summary. The log append worked because the critic resolved the path itself.

description: SPEC.md asked for ring-down segments and THRESHOLDS.md asked for a causality test with a 0.2 pre/post amplitude threshold, but neither required a node to store samples BEFORE the step boundary. The analyst's ring-down array starts at t=0 and the verifier's window starts 0.2 s after its boundary, so zero pre-boundary samples exist and the causality check is uncomputable as specified.
how_caught: The critic returned INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS, reported the zero count of t<0 samples, and stated that its monotonic-decay proxy is consistent with causality but does not test it
resolution: Open and honest: causality is UNTESTED in this pilot, not passed. The spec should have required a pre-boundary margin (e.g. 2 s before the boundary) in responses.npz. PROCESS_REPORT.md must report this as a check the graph could not perform rather than one it passed.

description: critic/THRESHOLDS.md asserted that forming the transfer function as a strict same-step ratio to ch1111 would make an instrumental gain change cancel. That is wrong when the change is IN ch1111, which is exactly the case at the 5.4-to-5.5 Hz boundary: force x1.735 while accelerometer ch1112 moves only x1.096 and bolometer response x0.85, so median |H| falls x0.496 (A) and x0.451 (V) and 0.85/1.735 = 0.49 accounts for essentially all of it. Both nodes therefore carry a spurious step in |H| at 5.45 Hz that no ratio removes.
how_caught: The critic tested the orchestrator's premise numerically against ch1112 and the bolometer medians instead of accepting it, and separately showed the 7.4-to-7.5 Hz boundary behaves differently and is a real response change
resolution: Open, ranked 4th in the critic's reconciliation list. The 5.45 Hz step must be treated as instrumental in both nodes' |H|, and the analyst's 5.494 Hz mode sits immediately after it and is untagged, while the verifier tagged the 7.4269 Hz mode. Needs adjudication at reconciliation.

description: The verifier's modes.csv header text states that its pt_harmonic_flag uses multiples of 1.4 Hz, contrary to the corrected SPEC.md requirement of 1.39443 Hz. No flag value actually changes, because all distances to 1.4 Hz multiples also exceed the 0.05 Hz limit, but the stated convention is wrong.
how_caught: The critic read both nodes' modes.csv headers and compared their declared PT convention against the spec
resolution: No numerical consequence for this dataset; recorded because the convention would matter for a mode nearer a harmonic. To be noted in comparison.csv as a cosmetic disagreement.

description: The verifier's own median-|H| local maximum at 2.6 Hz has prominence 1.46, above the 1.25 threshold it declared for itself, yet 2.6 Hz is absent from its own mode list. Its 9.2 and 9.4 Hz local maxima were also left unscored.
how_caught: The critic recomputed the verifier's own peak-prominence criterion from its outputs and compared it against the verifier's published mode list
resolution: Open. An internal inconsistency in the verifier found by a third node reading its work, which is precisely what the critic exists for. Feeds the unmatched-mode disagreement ranked 1st for reconciliation.

description: Reconciliation's first two attempts to locate the step boundaries (reconcile/r6_boundaries.py, r6b_check.py) used a 0.5 s boxcar lock-in to compare the force-channel envelope at f_k against f_k+1. A 0.5 s window has a frequency resolution of about 2 Hz and cannot separate 4.4 Hz from 4.5 Hz, so the two envelopes were equal to within 0.4% everywhere and the 'crossing' was noise. The answer it produced was the exact opposite of the truth: it said data/steps.csv was right and both nodes were 6 s early, contradicting the analyst's E029 finding.
how_caught: An internal consistency check built into the replacement script: true boundaries must be exactly 250 s apart. The void method gave only 70% of spacings within 0.1 s of 250 s with 21 outliers beyond 1 s; the instantaneous-frequency method (reconcile/r6c_instfreq.py) gives 250.0003 s with robust sigma 0.037 s and 96% within 0.1 s.
resolution: Both earlier scripts marked void in their own docstrings rather than deleted. The measurement stands on r6c: steps.csv is LATE by 5.986 s (robust sigma 0.127), confirming E029; the verifier sits +0.117 s from the measured boundary and the analyst -0.434 s.

description: Reconciliation's first pulser-shape stack (reconcile/r5_pulser.py) reported a 6 to 13 sigma feature in the quiet-window bolometer stacks and I briefly read it as the heater pulse. It was baseline drift: the per-segment median baseline leaves low-frequency wander that the pre-pulse sigma underestimates, and the 14 s window folded in the next pulse 10 s later. The 'peak' sat at +11.9 s, nowhere near t=0, and the band means rose monotonically through the whole window with no step at the pulse.
how_caught: The shape itself was wrong for a pulse -- monotonic, extremum at the far end of the window -- and the replacement script (r5b) added the control that should have been there first: the same stack at a deliberately wrong phase, pulse times + 5 s. On-pulse and control came out indistinguishable in every band.
resolution: r5 marked void in its docstring. The corrected result is a null with a control: no heater pulse is detectable on tower-19 bolometers in any quiet window below about 0.3 mV, confirmed without stacking by single-channel peak excursions that match the +5 s control to within 5%.

description: Three of the analyst's twelve modes do not survive reconciliation. 2.527 Hz is on one channel (ch962, which has the largest raw excursions of the channels sampled, 39.8 mV against 7.6-19.7) and sits on the first grid point, where no local maximum is even definable. 5.494 Hz is not a local |H| maximum on ANY of the 52 channels in either node's data and median |H| falls monotonically through it -- it is the ch1111 gain step of E036. 8.285 Hz is a local maximum on only 10 of 52 channels in the analyst's own H.
how_caught: reconcile/r1_modes.py counted, for every unmatched mode, the channels showing a significant 3-point local maximum of |H| in EACH node's own data, and reconcile/r4b_gain.py established the 5.45 Hz boundary as a gain change.
resolution: 2.527 and 5.494 Hz withdrawn; 8.285 Hz demoted to tentative and kept out of the headline list. Recorded in results/comparison.csv with the test that settled each.

description: The analyst's ERA missed three real modes that are plainly present in its own transfer functions. 6.2184, 7.9209 and 8.5297 Hz were reported by the verifier only, and a significant local |H| maximum sits at each one on 44, 32 and 25 of the 52 channels in the ANALYST's own H -- more per-channel support than two modes the analyst did report and both nodes accepted (7.46 Hz on 4 of 52, 8.17 Hz on 4 of 52).
how_caught: The verifier found them independently; the critic showed both nodes' median-|H| maxima contain them; reconciliation then counted the per-channel support in the analyst's own data, which is where the omission becomes undeniable.
resolution: All three accepted into the reconciled mode list. The analyst's ERA pole-stability criterion is the suspect, not its transfer functions. Not re-run: it would cost more than the pilot has, and the modes are established without it.

description: Cross-method agreement turned out not to be sufficient. The 7.43-7.46 Hz mode was found by BOTH nodes with independent methods and matched at 0.037 Hz separation, and it is still not established: it sits on the 7.45 Hz boundary, which reconciliation resolved as a gain change in both reference channels PLUS a genuine change in the force-to-acceleration relation, with the two drive monitors disagreeing by a factor 5 about what the drive did. Its per-channel support is also the weakest of any agreed mode, 4 of 52.
how_caught: reconcile/r4b_gain.py separated gain from physics by asking whether each channel's OFF-TONE noise scaled with its tone, which neither node nor the critic had tried; the mode's weak per-channel support came out of r1_modes.py.
resolution: Mode demoted despite the agreement. The process lesson is recorded for PROCESS_REPORT.md: two nodes sharing an instrument share its artefacts, so agreement between them bounds method error, not instrumental error. Both nodes referenced ch1111, which is exactly the channel at fault.

description: results/DEMO_NOTES.md described rec_01_graph as holding '~6 min' of live content and instructed the editor to cut everything after 6:00. Measured from the cast, the segment has 6,178 events and 25.5 minutes with no gap longer than a minute, and the material after 6:00 is the best in it: the verifier explaining the isolation boundary in its own words, the ledger on screen at 26 then 30 entries, live per-node token accounting, and the only human gate recorded before stop point 4. The cut list would have discarded all of it.
how_caught: Vivek asked whether the logs and recordings convey a coherent workflow, which prompted an actual frame-by-frame audit of all three casts instead of a reread of my own notes about them. The notes had been written from where I placed the === markers, not from what rendered.
resolution: Cut list rewritten against rendered frames with twelve timestamped entries; only two static stretches (12:30-21:00, 36:00-41:00) are now marked for trimming. Same root cause as E031 -- reasoning about a recording from something other than the recording.

description: verify/SPEC.md was never re-synced after SPEC.md was corrected. The verifier's copy was written at 04:24:19 UTC and the root copy was last edited at 04:59:58, after the verifier had already finished at 04:58:11, so the node ran to completion against a stale spec and the divergence then sat unnoticed for eight hours. Six substantive differences, the material ones being the pulse-tube fundamental (its copy said 1.4 Hz, the corrected root says 1.39443 Hz), the band (2.52-9.52 against 2.50-9.50), the aux channel count (71 against 78), and the entire force-discontinuity section, which its copy replaced with the superseded and wrong 'drive is constant, varies ~25% across frequency' text from E023. The log entry at line 1000 asserts the two copies were 'verified byte-identical' without noting that the claim was only true at dispatch.
how_caught: Vivek approved the SPEC 4.3 damping amendment and instructed that it be applied to BOTH copies. Diffing them before editing, rather than editing each in place, exposed the drift. Had the amendment been applied blind to each file the stale copy would have been carried into the re-dispatch.
resolution: verify/SPEC.md replaced with the amended SPEC.md and verified byte-identical by md5. Two earlier ledger entries are retracted in consequence, see E046 and E047. Standing rule added: the two spec copies are compared by checksum immediately before any node dispatch, not once at the start.

description: RETRACTION of E037's attribution. E037 recorded the verifier's modes.csv header declaring a 1.4 Hz pulse-tube convention as a verifier error, 'contrary to the corrected SPEC.md requirement of 1.39443 Hz'. The verifier's own spec copy said 1.4 Hz, as V019 of its log shows it faithfully applying. The node complied exactly with the document it held. The error was the orchestrator's failure to re-sync the copy (E045), and the critic's finding, while correct against the root spec, pointed at the wrong party.
how_caught: Found while diffing the two spec copies before applying the approved damping amendment
resolution: E037 left in place per the append-only rule; its node_that_erred should be read as orchestrator, not verifier. Verifier error count drops from 3 to 2. No numerical consequence: every mode is further than 0.05 Hz from a harmonic of both 1.4 and 1.39443 Hz, which is why this survived to now.

description: UNDER-CREDIT of the verifier, found in the same pass. E036, the finding that a strict same-step ratio to ch1111 cannot cancel a gain change located in ch1111 itself, was logged as caught by the critic. The verifier had already established it independently and more thoroughly at V020 of its own log, testing the orchestrator's premise against THREE independent witness channels (ch1112, ch1105, ch1107) and stating plainly that the ratio 'does not cancel, and in fact directly imports, a change in the CALIBRATION of ch1111 itself'. It then carried the consequence into modes.csv as the ADJACENT_TO_CH1111_SCALE_DISCONTINUITY flag on 7.4269 Hz. The critic, which could read verify/, re-derived it afterwards.
how_caught: Reading VERIFIER_LOG.md properly while checking what the stale spec had and had not told the node
resolution: E036 left in place per the append-only rule; the verifier reached it first and independently and is credited here. This is the clearest instance in the pilot of a blind node correcting its supervisor's physics unprompted, and PROCESS_REPORT.md section 2 is updated to say so.

description: The header comment block of verify/damping.csv states 'Three of the eleven modes yielded a ring-down measurement; eight did not'. Its own table has SEVEN measured and FOUR non-detections, and its own [V034] verdict lines agree with the table. Three is the number of modes for which Route C, the rational-fraction pole, returned a value (3.4075, 6.2184, 8.7834), so the prose conflated two routes and then understated its own result.
how_caught: Counted the rows of the delivered CSV against the prose in its own header before reading the narrative, and then against the per-mode [V034] verdict lines
resolution: The table and the [V034] lines are authoritative and agree; the header sentence is wrong and is flagged rather than edited, since the file is the node's own output. Same class as E038: a node's prose contradicting its own numbers, found by counting. Reported in comparison.csv.

description: Two full sets of [V034] per-mode verdicts were appended to VERIFIER_LOG.md and they disagree. The first calls 3.9707 Hz MEASURED with tau 12.32 +/- 0.44 s; the second calls it FAILED and reclassifies it as window-limited, and every tau error bar is widened by roughly a factor 3 to 6 (3.4075 Hz goes from +/-0.15 to +/-0.91 s). The node re-ran its aggregation with a more conservative error estimate and appended both without marking which supersedes which.
how_caught: Reading the log tail and noticing the same [V034] tags twice with different numbers, then checking which set damping.csv matches
resolution: Not a fault in the result: appending rather than overwriting is what the log rule requires, and the SECOND set is what damping.csv carries, with the wider and more honest error bars. Recorded so no reader quotes the superseded first set. The node should have labelled the supersession; the orchestrator states it here.

description: RETRACTION of the boundary verdict in results/comparison.csv. reconcile/r6c_instfreq.py smoothed the instantaneous frequency with a 1.0 s moving average and placed the boundaries at steps.csv minus 5.986 s, from which I concluded the verifier was accurate to +0.117 s and the analyst early by -0.434 s. The analyst, re-dispatched for causality, measured the boundaries independently with a two-segment changepoint scan and got steps.csv minus 6.356 s, 0.37 s from mine. Re-measuring with a 0.15 s average instead of 1.0 s gives steps.csv minus 6.227 s, so 0.24 s of my number was smoothing. The corrected boundary puts the ANALYST closest (0.06 to 0.19 s) and the verifier furthest (0.36 to 0.49 s), reversing what I published.
how_caught: The analyst measured the boundaries itself rather than accepting the orchestrator's figure, and reported the 0.37 s disagreement as an unresolved gap instead of quietly adopting either value. Two follow-up tests settled it: r6d_bias.py showed the estimator is unbiased on an IDEAL step (+0.000 s), which ruled out a coding error, and r6e_width.py showed the real transition is sharp at 0.048 s, which ruled out the ramp explanation and left over-smoothing as the cause.
resolution: comparison.csv row corrected and marked as a retraction; r6c annotated. The analyst was right twice: its original boundaries were closer to the truth than my correction to them, and its refusal to absorb my number is what exposed this. Residual 0.13 s is inside the analyst's own quoted sigma of 0.147 s.

description: Causality cannot be established per cell on this run. The analyst stored pre-boundary samples as amended SPEC 4.5 requires and ran the test: median pre/post amplitude ratio 0.049 against a null_far/post of 0.052, and a median pre/null_far ratio of 0.98. The pre-boundary signal IS the estimator's noise floor, so the measurement neither shows nor excludes a pre-response at the per-cell level. About 11% of cells exceed the 0.2 threshold even in the nulls, so the threshold is noise-limited rather than physics-limited.
how_caught: The analyst built two nulls of its own (null_far at 130 s before the boundary, null_mirror at a reflected frequency) and compared its result against them instead of against zero, which is what made the non-result visible as a non-result
resolution: Reported as INCONCLUSIVE per cell, not as a pass and not as a failure. What CAN be supported: on strong channels (post amplitude above 50x the floor, n=660) the median ratio is 0.010 with 0.9% of cells above 0.2, and 68 of 70 boundaries are below 0.2 by median over trusted channels. The two exceptions, 4.10 and 4.20 Hz, have failing nulls too and sit 0.017 Hz from the 4.18329 Hz pulse-tube line, which is stationary across the switch. Partial and preliminary: one run, one axis, one tower.

description: I wrote 'keep all of it; 25 of its 25 minutes are live' into results/DEMO_NOTES.md for rec_04_damping without measuring it. Measured, the segment has 3.5 live minutes of 24.9: a headless node prints nothing while it works, so the terminal sits idle between the dispatch and the result. This is the SAME mistake as E044, asserting a property of a recording from my expectation rather than from the file, committed two phases after logging E044 and writing the lesson 'check the screen, not your own notes about the screen'.
how_caught: Recomputing the live-content statistic for all six casts while updating TIMELINE.md with the two new phases, rather than carrying forward the number I had written
resolution: DEMO_NOTES.md and TIMELINE.md corrected to 3.5 live minutes of 24.9, with a note that the markers and the dispatch are what matter in that segment. Recorded prominently because a lesson logged and then repeated is more informative than one logged once: the fix for E044 was a corrected document, not a changed habit, and only a measurement caught it again.

description: RETRACTION of the r4b_gain.py interpretation. I concluded that the 5.45 Hz step was a pure instrumental gain change because ch1111's off-tone noise scaled with its tone (x1.836 against x1.729, ratio 0.94), and that 7.45 Hz was a gain change PLUS real physics because there the ratio moved x0.37. Two defects. First, r4b's off-tone band was 0.5-100 Hz with only the 2nd and 3rd harmonics removed, so every harmonic from the 4th up stayed in it; those scale with the drive, making off-tone track the tone BY CONSTRUCTION. Second, and fatal to the method, the off-tone is not a stable reference at all: ch1111's jumps beyond 5 sigma at 20 of 70 boundaries, often up and straight back down, because the shaker is a broadband source and the rig's mechanical noise responds to it. Redone with a drive-free 30-45 Hz band notched at all 60 harmonics, the tone/noise ratio change is x1.14 at 5.45 and x0.86 at 7.45 -- neither a clean pure-scale signature nor a clean tone-only one, and the 7.45 result reverses sign relative to what I published.
how_caught: Vivek asked 'so the gain change according to you is some instrumental error?'. Testing the premise instead of restating it meant looking at whether the off-tone behaves like a noise floor across the whole band, which it does not.
resolution: The INTERPRETATION is withdrawn; the downstream physics decisions survive on other evidence. What is defensible is narrower and method-independent: at 5.4->5.5 Hz the two drive monitors disagree by x1.58 (ch1111 tone x1.73, ch1112 x1.10) and at 7.4->7.5 Hz by x4.7 (x0.66 against x3.11), so |H| referenced to ch1111 is reference-dependent at those boundaries at that level and any mode adjacent to them is unreliable. Whether the cause is an instrument range change or a physical drive-point effect is NOT established. The 5.494 Hz withdrawal stands on the independent fact that 0 of 52 channels show a local |H| maximum there; the 7.46 Hz demotion stands on the monitor disagreement plus its 4-of-52 peak support.
